verdicts.flaw_description: The report states that every shop refitted its machines with a faster insert grade that same quarter and that every logged run was cut on one of those machines, so the faster inserts are an alternative cause fitting all four 4-7 minute reductions; the closing claim that 'no other change was made to any run' contradicts this.

The claim is about ward infection rates, but the measured quantity is 'culture requests' (6-11 percent below the prior quarter), which counts tests ordered rather than infections; a drop in test-ordering behaviour would produce the same numbers with no change in actual infection rate.

Premium stock's shelf share doubled to a record over the same period and 'every line was stocked straight from that shelf', so a richer premium product mix explains the 4-7 percent rise in revenue per order for all four lines independently of the pricing rule.

Two of the four cases have measurement dates preceding the intervention: cohort One 'started 4 April' but was measured 'by 29 March', and cohort Three 'started 5 October' but was measured 'by 30 September', so those heart-rate drops occurred before the app was used.
